reader_notes: Read by hand from the note text (dump.ts, bars 1-32), independently: no external analysis consulted. Beats are eighths, nine to the bar. x = the right hand's bar 1: the G-major arpeggio G4 B4 D5 B4 G4 D5 B4 G4 and the octave leap to G5, falling to F#5 at 2:1 (one bar). y = what the leader plays next (2:1-2:9): a quarter on F#5 and falling broken triads D5 A5 F#5 D5 A5 F#5 D5 (its second half has x's own 'down a third, up a fifth' shape). z = the scale-plus-arpeggio figure of 7:1 (B4 C5 D5 E5 B4 G5 E5 B4 G5); w = its partner in the bass, a half note and a falling turn (G3, F#3 E3 D3 E3 C#3). v = the broken-chord figure of 18:1 (E5 C5 A4, A5 E5 C5 A4, B4 C5). openings.ts gave the first imitation correctly (bass at 2:1 on D, 9 beats later); it stops at 2:9 because the answer is tonal.

leader.material: x, then y (2:1-2:9), then free broken chords of G7 in y's figure (bar 3)

first_imitation.changes: tonal: the leader's octave leap G4-G5 falling to F#5 becomes a seventh D3-C4 falling to B3 (3:1), so the answer turns back to G instead of going on to A; the arpeggio itself is exact.

opening.leader_meanwhile: canon: the leader goes on with y (on D) while the bass answers x; the bass then copies y as well, a twelfth lower on G (3:1-3:9), exact.
opening.canon_strict_to: 3:9 (bar 4: the leader's bar 3, G7 broken chords, is not copied; both voices start a sequence)
opening.notes: The bass is silent in bar 1. y's head (a long note and a falling third) comes back, reduced to two dotted quarters, against every later entry of x in bars 14-17.

voices.0: x (G), y (on D), free G7 broken chords in y's figure
voices.1: rest; x answered on D (tonal, 7th leap); y on G

members.reason: The bass states x on D (14:1, with the leader's octave leap D3-D4 falling to C#4) while the right hand holds D5; the right hand answers on A at 15:1 with the tonal seventh (A4 ... G5 falling to F#5), exactly as the prime's bass answered. y is reduced to its head in dotted quarters (bass C#4 A3 at 15:1). Where the prime's third bar gives y to the follower, the bass instead restarts x on D (16:1): see statements.

Tonic return. The right hand states x on G (27:1) and at once x on D in its answer form (28:1, seventh leap to C6 falling to B5): the leader carries both its own line and the follower's. The bass doubles each x one eighth later, two octaves down (G2 B2 D3 B2 G2 D3 B2 G2 at 27:2-9; D2 F#2 A2 F#2 D2 A2 F#2 D2 at 28:2-9), each preceded by a third (B2, F#2): a stretto at the fifteenth at one eighth. y is absent. Counted as a member because it restates the opening pair of entries G-D in the tonic; unsure, since the bass's line is x, not y: it may better be called a statement pair in stretto.

voices.1: w (half note, falling turn): G3 F#3 E3 D3 E3 C#3; F#3 E3 D3 C#3 D3 B2

prime.key: G/e to D, one-bar units down by step

members.reason: The bass takes z exactly (E3 F#3 G3 A3 E3 C#4 A3 E3 C#4), the right hand takes w with its turn starting a step above the held note (G4, A4 G4 F#4 G4 E4) instead of below it. The pattern goes no further: bar 10 begins the approach to D with new figures. Unsure whether a one-bar exchange inside a sequence should count as a member; the alternative is to read 7-13 as one elaboration with an internal exchange.

Bass C3 held from 24:1 moves to D3 (26:2); right hand E4 to F#4 on a plain D chord. Unsure: the D chord takes its seventh (C3 at 26:7) and runs on into I6 at 27:1, so it may be read as a dominant preparation rather than a cadence. Review: the bass holds C3 from 24:1 and reaches D3 at 26:2, so the arrival on V is at 26:2.

layout.form: rounded bipartite (central PAC in V at 14:1, tonic return at 27). Alternative: tripartite 1-14 / 14-26 / 27-32, but the third part is half the length of the others.

also: motivic-sequential (most of the elaboration is one-bar sequences of broken chords)

notes: Sure: the tonal answer at 2:1, the brief canon of x and y, the PAC in D at 14:1, the chain of x entries D-A-D-G (14-17), the tonic return at 27 in stretto at one eighth, the final PAC. Unsure: whether bars 7-9 make a paradigm (beta) or an elaboration with one exchange; whether 7:1 (IAC) and 26 (HC) are cadences; whether bars 27-28 are a member of alpha or two statements in stretto; the primary kind (fugal vs motivic-sequential). x is a full bar long, not 'half a bar or less', which is why fugal is preferred. No real inversion of x occurs.
